extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers of systematic reviews of interventions (Cochrane review authors, evidence synthesis researchers, guideline developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing and appraising Cochrane-style systematic reviews of healthcare interventions, including protocol development, study identification, risk-of-bias assessment, data synthesis, and presentation of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol development and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and register a protocol that specifies objectives, eligibility criteria, outcomes, methods for study selection, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, and planned analyses before starting the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol should be publicly available (e.g., PROSPERO/Cochrane Register). Pre-specifying methods reduces bias from post hoc decisions; justify any deviations from protocol and report them transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear eligibility criteria (PICO/PS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria for participants, interventions, comparisons, outcomes, study designs, settings, and time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify population characteristics (age, condition), intervention details (dose, duration), comparator(s), primary and secondary outcomes (including time points), eligible study designs (e.g., RCTs only), and any language or publication status limits. Explain rationale for choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a sensitive, reproducible search strategy across appropriate bibliographic databases, trial registries, grey literature, and other sources to identify all relevant studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search multiple databases (e.g., CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase), use both controlled vocabulary and free-text terms, search trial registries and conference proceedings, check references and citation lists, contact experts/authors, and document dates, search strings, and limits. Avoid unjustified language or publication-status restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply eligibility criteria consistently to screen titles/abstracts and full texts, with procedures to reduce errors and bias in selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use at least two independent reviewers for screening and full-text assessment, record and report reasons for exclusions, present a flow diagram (PRISMA) showing numbers at each stage, and resolve disagreements by consensus or third reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract study data using standardized forms and procedures that minimize errors and capture all data needed for analyses and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use piloted data extraction forms, have at least two reviewers extract or verify data, extract study characteristics, intervention details, outcomes (including measures and time points), funding/conflicts, and risk-of-bias information. Contact study authors for missing or unclear data and document responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment for randomized trials (RoB domains)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess risk of bias in included randomized trials across standard domains: random sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding (participants/personnel and outcome assessment), incomplete outcome data, selective outcome reporting, and other sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make domain-level judgments (low/unclear/high) with supporting text explaining the basis. Use two independent assessors and resolve disagreements. Consider impact of bias on results in interpretation and analyses (e.g., sensitivity analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment for non-randomized studies (ROBINS-I)
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-randomized studies of interventions, evaluate bias across domains relevant to non-randomized designs (confounding, selection into the study, classification of interventions, deviations from intended interventions, missing data, measurement of outcomes, selection of reported result).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a structured tool (e.g., ROBINS-I) to judge risk-of-bias in relation to a hypothetical target trial; provide domain-level and overall judgments and justify them. Consider confounding and selection biases carefully when including non-randomized evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures of treatment effect and outcome metric selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select appropriate effect measures for each outcome (e.g., risk ratio, odds ratio, risk difference for dichotomous outcomes; mean difference or standardized mean difference for continuous outcomes; rate ratios or hazard ratios for time-to-event outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer measures that are clinically interpretable and consistent across studies. Convert scales where appropriate or use standardized measures when different instruments measure the same construct. Report effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with multiple intervention groups and unit-of-analysis issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle trials with more than two intervention groups, cluster-randomized trials, crossover trials, and other unit-of-analysis complexities appropriately in synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid double-counting participants (e.g., combine groups or split comparator groups), account for clustering (use adjusted analyses or effective sample sizes), and for crossover trials use paired analyses where possible or include only first-period data if carryover likely. Clearly report methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and address missing outcome data at study and participant levels and consider the potential impact on results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract how trials handled missing data, prefer analyses based on intention-to-treat where appropriate, perform sensitivity analyses exploring assumptions about missing data (best/worst-case, imputations), and transparently report the potential for bias from missingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and interpretation of heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess clinical, methodological, and statistical heterogeneity among included studies and consider implications for pooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore heterogeneity qualitatively (differences in populations, interventions, outcomes) and quantitatively using Chi-squared test and I-squared statistic (reporting I^2 and its uncertainty) and Tau^2. Interpret I^2 with attention to number of studies, effect sizes, and CIs; avoid relying solely on arbitrary thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of synthesis model: fixed-effect vs random-effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide and justify whether to use fixed-effect or random-effects meta-analysis models based on the review question and expected between-study variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random-effects models account for heterogeneity in true effects and are often appropriate when studies differ clinically; report model chosen, rationale, and consider sensitivity analyses comparing models. Be cautious interpreting random-effects pooled estimates when few studies or substantial heterogeneity exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis conduct and pooling methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct meta-analyses using appropriate statistical methods for chosen effect measures, weighting, and variance estimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inverse-variance methods or other appropriate pooling techniques, choose correct effect metric, handle zero-event studies with appropriate continuity corrections or alternative methods, and report pooled estimates with confidence intervals and measures of heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup and interaction analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specify and limit subgroup analyses to plausible hypotheses and test interactions rather than making conclusions from within-group significance alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report subgroups specified a priori in protocol, use formal statistical tests for subgroup differences, interpret cautiously due to multiple testing and low power, and avoid overinterpretation of post hoc subgroup findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct sensitivity analyses to test robustness of review findings to key decisions (e.g., risk-of-bias inclusion, choice of effect measure, analytic model, handling of missing data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify important sensitivity analyses where possible, report results and how they affect conclusions, and use them to assess credibility of pooled estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of reporting biases across studies (publication bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess potential for reporting biases, including publication bias, selective non-reporting, and small-study effects, and consider their impact on review conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contour-enhanced funnel plots and statistical tests for asymmetry when ≥10 studies; interpret cautiously as asymmetry can have many causes. Search grey literature and trial registries to reduce missing studies; consider impact on GRADE judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative synthesis when meta-analysis not appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When pooling is inappropriate, synthesize evidence narratively using structured methods to summarize study characteristics, direction and size of effects, and patterns across studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tables to present study-by-study results, group studies by key characteristics, explore reasons for differences, avoid vote counting on statistical significance alone, and discuss strength and consistency of evidence qualitatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing certainty of the body of evidence (GRADE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the certainty (quality) of the evidence for each important outcome using GRADE domains: risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and publication bias (and upgrading criteria where applicable for non-randomized evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start RCT evidence as high and downgrade for problems across domains; start observational evidence lower or use ROBINS-I as starting point for grading; present Summary of Findings tables with absolute and relative effects, number of participants/studies, and rationale for GRADE judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of results (figures and tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present study and synthesis results transparently using forest plots, Summary of Findings tables, risk-of-bias tables, and structured text summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include effect estimates with confidence intervals, heterogeneity statistics, clear labeling of outcomes and time points, and explanatory text about clinical importance and applicability. Use consistent units and scales across tables/figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting clinical importance vs statistical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the clinical relevance of effect sizes in addition to statistical significance, considering minimal important differences, baseline risks, and patient-relevant outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate relative effects into absolute effects using baseline risks; discuss whether observed differences are meaningful to patients and decision-makers; avoid equating non-significance with no effect when underpowered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with multiplicity and selective reporting within studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and consider the consequences of multiple outcomes, multiple time points, and selective reporting of favorable results within studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract all reported outcomes, compare protocols/registrations to publications when available, consider outcome-selection bias when judging risk of bias and GRADE, and clearly state which outcome/time point was the primary focus for the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching for and synthesizing adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and execute searches and data collection for harms/adverse effects, recognizing differences in how harms are reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broader and specialized search terms for adverse events, include observational evidence where appropriate, consider different definitions and ascertainment methods, and present harms separately with discussion of certainty and rarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of conflicts of interest and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and report funding sources and conflicts of interest for included studies and for review authors, and consider how these might bias study conduct, reporting, and review conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract study funding and author conflicts, report them in characteristics of included studies, discuss potential influence on findings, and declare review authors' conflicts and role of funders in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating and living reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for keeping the review up to date, including criteria for when to update and approaches for living systematic reviews when rapid evidence change is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify update triggers in the protocol, monitor new evidence, and for living reviews set processes for continuous search, screening, and incorporation of new data with transparent versioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reporting guidelines and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow established reporting standards (e.g., PRISMA) and provide sufficient information for reproducibility and appraisal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a structured abstract, detailed methods, full search strategies, list of excluded studies with reasons, data extraction forms or templates, and make analytic code/data available where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical considerations for rare events and zero cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply appropriate statistical approaches when events are rare or studies report zero events in one or both arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternative models (Peto OR, exact methods, beta-binomial, continuity corrections), report chosen method and its assumptions, and perform sensitivity analyses to test robustness to method choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating evidence from multiple study designs
rubrics_metrics.description: When combining RCTs and non-randomized studies, prespecify rationale and methods for integration and consider differences in bias and applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytically separate randomized and non-randomized evidence where appropriate, justify pooling across designs, explore consistency of effects, and reflect design-related differences in GRADE certainty judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software, reproducibility, and reporting of analytic choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate software (e.g., RevMan, GRADEpro, statistical packages) and report all analytic choices, code/scripts, and parameters to enable reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document software and versions, exact commands or settings for meta-analyses, models and priors if Bayesian methods used, and make data and code publicly available when possible.
